title: MORNING ACTION
intro: Crude at $100+ keeps Nifty bulls under pressure. Defend 23,000 or face deeper downside. Protect capital!
sourceNote: Transcribed from supplied videos, not verified current market data. Preserve source values, including inconsistencies between prose and table.

sections.title: Early Morning Insightful Analysis
sections.body:
THE BIG THEME | Nifty BULLS ON THE BACK FOOT

# BLAME IT ON – WTI AT $100; BRENT AT $112.50 | INFLATION RISKS INTENSIFY
Soaring crude caps recovery hopes as escalating Middle East tensions intensify risks to India’s inflation outlook, import bill and corporate margins.

# 🟢 TECHNICAL WATCH | BULLS NEED TO RECLAIM LOST GROUND

Watch 23,000, followed by 23,227, as recovery hurdles.

# THE BIG QUESTION – CAN BUYERS ARREST THE THREE-SESSION SLIDE?

# 🟢 DIPLOMACY WATCH
Only a credible progress towards de-escalation, backed by easing crude prices, could offer the bulls some relief.

# OUR CALL OF THE DAY | EXTREME CAUTION WARRANTED.

Upside could remain capped. Protect capital, avoid chasing rebounds and let sustained buying confirm the recovery.

insightsSections.title: BEFORE WE START | THURSDAY’S MARKET RECAP
insightsSections.body:
🔴 Dalal Street extended its losing streak to three sessions.

Surging crude and escalating Middle East tensions weighed on sentiment, while broader-market weakness highlighted fragile risk appetite.

🔴 SENSEX: 73,249 (−460 points).

🔴 BANK NIFTY: 54926 (−51 points).

insightsSections.title: WHAT’S NEXT FOR NIFTY | BULLS ON THE BACK FOOT
insightsSections.body:
Support: 22,500 / 22,180
Resistance: 23,000 / 23,227

🟢 Reclaiming and a sustained recovery above 23,000, followed by 23,227, needs heavyweight buying and stronger market breadth.

🔴 Failure to stabilise above 22,500 could expose 22,180.

Until participation improves, rebounds remain vulnerable to selling.

insightsSections.title: THE BIG HEADWIND | CRUDE FUELS INFLATION FEARS
insightsSections.body:
🔴 Brent around $112.50 a barrel raises concerns over imported inflation, corporate margins and India’s external balances.

Elevated energy costs could complicate the outlook for rate relief.
